clue.text: Class of worker secure in depression at first

indicators.note: this phrase says the word for depression stands at the front, ahead of the word for secure

parts.note: feeling blue means feeling low or depressed
to collar someone is to seize and hold them securely

explanation.surface: A labourer feels safely employed even though he is gloomy at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal but is only a link; 'at first' fixes the order of the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Manual workers are described by the phrase, from the overalls traditionally worn on the factory floor.

clue.text: Toiler with little change for loaf

indicators.note: the letters of the word toiler change places, yet only a little rearranging is needed

explanation.surface: A labourer slacks off with small pay in his pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: To loaf is to idle, hang about doing nothing.

clue.text: Aim to overcome displeasure by compromise

indicators.note: in a down clue, to overcome places the word for aim above the word for displeasure

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal
anger is strong displeasure

explanation.surface: A negotiator aims to resolve resentment by meeting halfway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compromise' is the verb meaning to put at risk, not the noun meaning a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To compromise safety or security is to put it at risk.

clue.text: Cultivated plot a scene of variegated colour display

indicators.note: cultivated means the letters of plot a scene are worked over into new order

explanation.surface: A tilled garden bed makes a bright, many-coloured show.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing shifting milky iridescent colours like a gem opal.

clue.text: Wycliffite nobleman holding up everything

indicators.note: holding says the nobleman contains the reversed word

parts.note: a lord is a nobleman

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for everything is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A follower of Wycliffe sees a peer stopping everything.
explanation.walkthrough: John Wycliffe was a 14th-century English church reformer whose followers were branded heretics; 'up' and 'holding' do the work, the reversal sitting inside the nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of the reformer John Wycliffe were given this name, a medieval heretic sect.

clue.text: Squabbles causing tears, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is spoken aloud and spelt another way

parts.note: a rose has thorns that rip, so it causes tears in clothing or skin

explanation.surface: Quarrels that bring someone to weeping, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tears' suggests weeping but means rips. The sound of ROSE gives ROWS spelt as lines; the definition reads it to rhyme with cows.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisy quarrels are rows, rhyming with cows, arguments and disputes.

clue.text: Half Joffre's call-up held the north in furious action

indicators.note: held says the abbreviation for north sits inside the rest
half picks the second half of the name Joffre
in a down clue, up means the word for call is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: to cite is to call or summon
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Marshal Joffre's mobilisation of half the army held the north amid frantic fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: Joffre was a French First World War commander, which gives the surface its military call-up; 'Half', 'up' and 'held' are the three working signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Frantic, wildly hectic, describing someone or something rushing about.

clue.text: Not to be swallowed, even when cigar ends removed

definitions.text: Not to be swallowed, even when cigar ends removed

parts.words: Not to be swallowed, even when cigar ends removed
parts.note: unbelievable means not to be swallowed as a story; drop C and R, the first and last letters of cigar, and the word left means not to be eaten

explanation.walkthrough: Taking C and R (the ends of 'cigar') out of the answer leaves INEDIBLE, which also means not to be swallowed.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall tale too far-fetched to believe cannot be swallowed, accepted as true.

clue.text: Make faster progress abroad with career

parts.note: out and abroad both mean away from home, outside
to career is to rush along, to run

explanation.surface: Someone advances faster by going overseas with their profession.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat another runner is to go quicker than them and leave them behind.

clue.text: Fruit drop or humbug before trip

indicators.note: before places the word for humbug ahead of the word for trip

parts.note: humbug is empty talk, hot air or wind
a trip is a stumble or fall

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a dropped fruit is real or just nonsense ahead of a stumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Apples blown off the tree by a gale are this, hence also a lucky gain.

clue.text: Inventory always including name of auditor

parts.note: an inventory is a list of items

indicators.note: including means the poetic word for always holds the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: An inventory always lists the name of the accountant who checked it.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor in the older sense is one who hears, a hearer.

clue.text: Run into large vessel

indicators.note: into says the abbreviation for run goes inside the word for large

parts.note: large means big
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Someone collides with a big ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-masted square-rigged sailing ship is a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Brook and ornamental grounds a scene of tumult

parts.note: to brook is to tolerate, to bear
a garden is ornamental grounds

explanation.surface: A stream and formal gardens are the setting for an uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brook' looks like a stream but is the verb meaning tolerate. Bear-baiting pits gave the name for any rowdy place.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a place for bear-baiting, hence any rowdy or chaotic assembly.

clue.text: Lad on French horse cleared obstacle

parts.note: sur is the French word for on
a mount is a horse for riding
Ed is a lad's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: A stable boy riding a French horse jumped a fence.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'Lad on' a rider; in fact 'on French' gives SUR, and the boy's name ED goes on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To get over a difficulty is to overcome it, the sense of the past-tense verb here.

clue.text: Ordered aid to enter established position

indicators.note: ordered means the letters of aid to enter are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Help was instructed to go in and set up camp.
explanation.definitionFit: Having got one's bearings, one has worked out where one stands.

clue.text: Builds up to a sea journey reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly says the words are heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a cruise is a sea journey, so these words give A CRUISE

explanation.surface: Something mounts up the way a voyage at sea does, so they say.
explanation.definitionFit: Interest or debt that gathers over time is said to grow, to accumulate.

clue.text: Our price slashed, but he gets the rake-off

indicators.note: slashed means the letters of our price are cut up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cut in the price still leaves someone their cut of the profits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rake-off' suggests a dishonest cut; the casino attendant literally rakes in the chips.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino attendant collects the stakes at the table with a long rake.

clue.text: Motorway turning restriction catches policing centre vehicle

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first motorway, with the 1 written as I

indicators.note: catches says the reversed restriction holds those middle letters inside it
turning means the word for restriction is read backwards

parts.note: a ban is a restriction

indicators.note: centre picks the middle two letters of the word policing

explanation.surface: A ban on turning on the motorway traps a police car at the centre.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, so 'Motorway' gives MI; 'turning', 'catches' and 'centre' are the other signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A small taxi booked by phone is a car for hire, a passenger vehicle.

clue.text: Encourage one to enter climbing expeditions to Northern Ireland

indicators.note: to enter says the numeral for one goes inside the reversed pieces
in a down clue, climbing means both pieces are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: trips are expeditions
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Climbers are urged to join mountain expeditions in Ulster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns both pieces at once in this down clue, giving INSPIRT, before 'to enter' slips the numeral in.
explanation.definitionFit: To fill someone with spirit and courage, to hearten them.

clue.text: Articles in support of company neckwear, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue, in support of places the articles beneath the word for company

parts.note: a band is a company of people
an and a are the indefinite articles
an and a are the indefinite articles

explanation.surface: Clothing items are backed by a firm making scarves.
explanation.definitionFit: A brightly coloured handkerchief worn around the neck or head is a type of scarf.

clue.text: Commercial traveller sticking to established lines?

definitions.text: Commercial traveller sticking to established lines?

parts.words: Commercial traveller sticking to established lines?
parts.note: it looks like a sales rep who keeps to a routine, but read it as a carrier of merchandise that runs along fixed railway tracks

explanation.walkthrough: A commercial traveller is a salesman on the road; here 'commercial' means freight and 'lines' are railway tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: A freight service carries merchandise by rail along laid tracks.

clue.text: Camp boundary

definitions.meaning: a camp is a faction or party in a dispute
a boundary is an edge or flank

explanation.definitionFit: A team or party in a contest, and also the edge or border of something.

clue.text: Repudiate girl over broadcast

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the girl above the word for broadcast

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
broadcast seed is scattered, sown

explanation.surface: Someone rejects a woman after a radio programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' suggests radio but means scattered, as seed is.
explanation.definitionFit: To renounce or refuse to acknowledge as one's own.

clue.text: Left in the long grass but brought back

indicators.note: in says the word for left sits inside the word for long grass

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass growing in water
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Something lost in the long grass was eventually retrieved.
explanation.definitionFit: News that is relayed or carried back to someone has been passed on, announced.

clue.text: A dynasty with taste?

definitions.meaning: the ... were a Chinese imperial dynasty

explanation.surface: A ruling family with refined taste.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese imperial line of the 7th-10th centuries, and also a sharp distinctive flavour.

clue.text: Subsidiary accommodation requiring a rent arrangement with low return

indicators.note: arrangement means the letters of a rent are rearranged
return means the word for low is read backwards

parts.note: to low is to moo like a cow

explanation.surface: A small extra room comes with a rental deal that pays little back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' turns A RENT into ANTER; 'return' makes OOM from MOO.
explanation.definitionFit: A small room leading into a larger one is a secondary space, a waiting room.

clue.text: 21, perhaps, in the Spanish plane

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
plane in the sense of flat, level, even

explanation.surface: Someone sits in seat 21 of a Spanish aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' looks like an aircraft but is the adjective meaning flat. 21 across means a team, and a cricket or football team has this many players.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket or football team consists of this many players, so a team can be called by the number.

clue.text: Splendid viewpoint given by August weather

parts.note: august means majestic, grand
to weather a storm is to stand up to it

explanation.surface: A fine summer day provides a wonderful view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'August' with its capital looks like the month, but it is the adjective meaning majestic.
explanation.definitionFit: The main covered seating at a sports ground gives the best view of play.
